exercise.name: Band Twist (Up-Down)

reference.title: Band twist (up-down)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment, so the data sheet was not read; the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching: a high-to-low chop)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (trunk rotation with a diagonal arm pull)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull the band down and across, breathe in as the arms return up to the anchor.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s down, 1.5 s back up

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of losing control of the return (clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Band tension is user-chosen: step farther from the anchor for more tension
prescription.progression: Stronger band, slower return, half-kneeling version for more trunk control

cues.text: Stand side-on to the anchor, band tied high on the upright. Feet a little wider than the hips, knees soft. Turn toward the anchor and reach up to it with both hands on the handle, arms long.
Breathe out and pull the band down and across the body to the outside of the far hip, turning the ribs and hips together, arms long.
Brief pause low; chest up, knees soft, feet planted.
Let the arms rise back up to the anchor slowly, turning back as one piece.
Reach tall toward the anchor, then chop again. Turn around to train the other side.

mistakes.fix: Turn the ribs and hips together; the arms stay long and guide the band.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back at the bottom
mistakes.fix: Soften the knees and hips a little; chest stays up.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the band yank the arms back up

mistakes.fix: Keep both feet planted; the hips turn over them.

kinematics.norm: Ribs and hips turn together from facing the anchor to facing away; mostly thoracic and hip rotation (clinical opinion; end-range twisting under flexion is the concern, Marshall and McGill 2010)
Diagonal from above the near shoulder to outside the far hip (clinical opinion)
Soft knees, a little more bend low (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Torso-twist exercise with elastic resistance vs a training machine: core muscle EMG (Scientifica 2015:403068; PubMed 26557405)
Oliva-Lozano and Muyor 2020, core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306)
Marshall and McGill 2010, the role of axial torque in disc herniation (Clin Biomech 25:6-9), porcine model

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Check the band and the anchor before each set: a band that slips or snaps can hit you, and it passes near the face at the top.
Keep the range comfortable and turn the hips with the ribs; avoid a forceful end-range twist with a rounded back (Marshall and McGill 2010).
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low back discomfort: smaller turn, more knee bend, or a half-kneeling chop.
Shoulder discomfort: start lower on the upright (chest height).
regressions: Lighter band or stand closer to the anchor.

muscleNotes.obliques_r: Turn the trunk down and across against the band (oblique pair across the trunk). In elastic-band torso twists the external oblique reached about 54-77% MVC (Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Turn the trunk down and across against the band (Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis helps pull the ribs down toward the far hip; transversus braces (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Pull the long arms down from overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Pull the long arms down from overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Keep the elbows long; the long head helps pull the arm down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Keep the elbows long; the long head helps pull the arm down (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Turn and steady the pelvis over the planted feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Turn and steady the pelvis over the planted feet (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the chest up as the hands go low (erector spinae about 32-50% MVC in torso twists, Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the chest up as the hands go low (Scientifica 2015).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Hold the soft knee bend (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Hold the soft knee bend (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Help the arm sweep down and across (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Help the arm sweep down and across (clinical opinion).
